answer: Joining burns a floating fee. Each identity pays a yarrow-stamped fee of 10 credits at the bridge; every 10 joins lift the fee one terrace, 2 credits. The fee is destroyed, never staked, so capital cannot fund two identities. A flood of 1,000 fakes burns about 110,000 in one epoch, the last over 200 each, more than the whole 40,000-credit pool. Auditors recompute the ladder from the public log, so spacing joins fails. An honest agent pays 10.
